dform.name: Name
dform.ecHint: On save, one tag is auto-created per address. Digital inputs/coils become COUNTER tags (assign role + machine in the Tags screen).
dform.ecEditNote: Block ranges are set at creation and are read-only here — add/remove tags in the Tags screen.
dform.deleteDesc: This will permanently delete this device and all related data.

tform.counterMapping: Counter mapping — +1 per edge, applied to the machine's running Job Order
tform.etTotalizerHint: The device counts the pulses itself and the gateway reads a running total. Use this when the pulse is too short to be seen reliably — the count no longer depends on how often the tag is polled.
tform.machineStatusDriver: Machine status driver (drives RUNNING / IDLE / stop)
tform.processingNeverDrivesState: A processing signal never drives machine state: it measures whether product is flowing, which is what Starved and Blocked are inferred from. Read as a state it would call every gap between units a fault.
tform.deadbandHelp: In 'On change' mode, only emit when the value moves by at least this much. Leave blank for any change.
tform.boolHelp: BOOL: true → RUNNING; false → BREAKDOWN (unplanned stop) when a job order is in progress, else IDLE.
tform.intHelp: INT: value → state. Leave the map empty to use the standard 0-based default (0 IDLE · 1 RUNNING · 2 BREAKDOWN · 3 PLANNED_STOP · 4 SETUP · 5 CHANGEOVER · 6 STARVED · 7 BLOCKED · 8 OFFLINE · 9 MAINTENANCE).
tform.deleteDesc: This will permanently delete this tag and all historical data.
tform.roleRunMode: Run Mode — ON = running or ready
tform.roleProcessing: Processing — product is actually being worked
tform.roleNoneHelp: Read literally through the status map above. No extra interpretation.
tform.roleRunModeHelp: ON means the machine is running OR ready with nothing to do. Pair it with a Processing signal to tell those apart, otherwise waiting counts as running.
tform.roleRunModePulsedHelp: Steady ON = running, pulsing = stopped, OFF = alarm. Used where the machine signals a stop by blinking rather than by opening the contact.
tform.roleProcessingHelp: Distinguishes working from waiting. Without it a machine that is ready but starved is indistinguishable from one that is producing.
tform.roleInfeedHelp: OFF while the machine is stopped is read as Starved. Takes precedence over inference from neighbouring machines.
tform.roleOutfeedHelp: ON while the machine is stopped is read as Blocked. Takes precedence over inference from neighbouring machines.
tform.pulseHelp: Pulsing is declared when at least this many transitions occur inside the window. Set the window to a few pulse periods so one missed poll does not read as steady.
tform.idleThresholdHelp: How long this signal must stay inactive before the machine counts as waiting rather than mid-cycle. Set it to the slowest normal cycle for this machine — too short reports starvation between every unit.

rules.title: Signal Interpretation
rules.subtitle: How a wire becomes a state, and what that state costs in downtime and OEE.
rules.noSignals: No status signals are bound yet. Set a signal interpretation on a tag in the Tag Browser first — until then machine state is read literally from the status map.
rules.empty: No rules. The gateway falls back to its built-in defaults.
rules.deleteDesc: A per-machine rule falls back to the factory rule. Deleting the factory rule falls back to the gateway default, so downtime is still recorded either way.
rules.precedenceHelp: A rule for a specific machine wins over the factory-wide rule for the same state, which wins over the gateway built-in default. So one machine can be treated differently without changing the rest.
rules.isDowntimeHelp: Entering this state starts a downtime record, closed when the machine leaves it.
rules.isPlannedHelp: Marks the event as planned. Reporting separates planned from unplanned loss.
rules.affectsOeeHelp: Off means the time is recorded but removed from the availability denominator — for losses caused outside this machine, such as waiting for material. Off flatters the machine, so use it only when the cause genuinely is not its own.
rules.debounceHelp: How long the state must hold before it is believed. Guards against a flickering contact filling the downtime log with one-second events. 0 records immediately.
rules.noAlarms: No alarm rules configured. Nothing on a tag value will raise an alarm until one is added.
rules.deleteAlarmDesc: The rule stops firing. Its past events are kept — an alarm history that vanishes when a rule is edited is not a history.
rules.alarmSaveFailed: Could not save the alarm rule
rules.alarmDeleteFailed: Could not delete the alarm rule
rules.alarmEngineHelp: Evaluated at the edge on every reading, so a crossing between two API polls is not missed and alarms keep firing while the link to the server is down.
rules.deadbandHelp: Once raised, the value must come back past the threshold by this much before the alarm clears. Blank means it clears the moment the condition is false — which makes a value sitting on the limit chatter.
rules.delayHelp: The condition must hold continuously this long before an event is raised. A momentary spike is not a fault.
rules.autoAckHelp: For informational alarms nobody is expected to action. Keeps them out of the operator queue.
rules.activeHelp: Switch off to stop the rule firing without deleting it, so its history survives.
rules.bindSignalTitle: Bind a signal to its meaning
rules.bindableHelp: Only boolean points are listed. A role on an analogue register would be read as "is it 1 or more", which is not what a run contact means.
rules.signalSaveFailed: Could not save the signal interpretation
